citation.authors: Lynch G, Nieto K, Puthenveettil S, Reyes M, Jureller M, Huang JH, Grady MS, Harris OA, Ganju A, Germano IM, Pilitsis JG, Pannullo SC, Benzil DL, Abosch A, Fouke SJ, Samadani U
citation.title: Attrition rates in neurosurgery residency: analysis of 1361 consecutive residents matched from 1990 to 1999

study_period: Match years 1990-1999; followed to board certification (study published 2014/15)
cohort: 1361 residents matched via SF Match (146 women, 1215 men)
data_source: SF Match lists; ABNS Directory of Diplomates (board certification); AMA DoctorFinder and NPI for practice status
method: Retrospective matched-cohort tracing of each matched individual
attrition_definition: Non-completion of residency (secondary: non-board-certification). Abstract does not state how in-specialty transfers that completed elsewhere were handled; completion appears to be person-level (completed any NS residency) - verify in full text.
counts_transfers: unclear from abstract (person-level completion suggests transfers who completed are NOT attrition)

headline_rates.by_program: not in abstract; board certification by med school type: public 82.2%, private 77.1%, international 77.8%

key_findings: Women significantly more at risk of not completing residency or not becoming board certified (p<0.005). Public medical school alumni had higher board-certification rates than private/international. No difference by top-10 school. 0.2% deceased, 0.3% lost to follow-up.

citation.authors: Renfrow JJ, Rodriguez A, Liu A, Pilitsis JG, Samadani U, Ganju A, Germano IM, Benzil DL, Wolfe SQ
citation.title: Positive trends in neurosurgery enrollment and attrition: analysis of the 2000-2009 female neurosurgery resident cohort

data_source: AANS and ABNS databases matched against graduation records; internet search for non-graduates
method: Retrospective cohort; primary outcome = women not completing NS training
attrition_definition: Did not complete neurosurgery training (graduation not reported from NS residency programs). Handling of within-specialty transfers not stated in abstract.

headline_rates.by_PGY: majority of leavers left within first 3 years (abstract; no %)

key_findings: Leavers mostly stayed in medicine (anesthesia, neurology, radiology). Female attrition comparable to other surgical specialties but higher than male NS attrition. Note: the title of this paper is 'Positive trends in neurosurgery enrollment and attrition' (J Neurosurg), not World Neurosurg as the task prompt guessed. Commentary: Robinson S, 'The best and the brightest', PMID 26452120; reply Wolfe SQ PMID 27358956.

citation.authors: Agarwal N, White MD, Pannullo SC, Chambless LB
citation.title: Analysis of national trends in neurosurgical resident attrition

data_source: AANS resident data; internet search for non-completers
method: Retrospective cohort; outcomes classified as transferred NS program / different specialty / left clinical medicine / deceased / unknown
attrition_definition: Did not finish residency at the program in which they started. EXPLICITLY INCLUDES transfers to another NS program (33.61% of attrition group) and deaths (1.68%).

headline_rates.overall: 10.98% (no significant difference across start years, p=0.337)
headline_rates.by_PGY: 65.07% of attrition in PGY-1 or PGY-2
headline_rates.attrition_group_outcomes: 33.61% transferred NS programs; 56.30% different specialty; 8.40% left clinical medicine; 1.68% deceased
headline_rates.approx_our_definition: Rough back-calculation (not stated by authors): excluding NS transfers and deaths (~35% of attrition group) implies ~7% non-completion of NS - derived, not reported

key_findings: Attrition group older at start (31.69 vs 29.31 y, p<0.001). Leavers went mostly to neurology, radiology, anesthesiology. Risk factors: older age, female sex, junior PGY.

citation.authors: Yaeger KA, Munich SA, Byrne RW, Germano IM
citation.title: Trends in United States neurosurgery residency education and training over the last decade (2009-2019)

cohort: All ACGME NS residents (1112 -> 1462 residents over decade)
data_source: ACGME Data Resource Books, NRMP, ABNS records, PubMed
method: Descriptive trend analysis of aggregate annual data
attrition_definition: Annual (cross-sectional) attrition from ACGME data; ACGME counts residents leaving a program (withdrawal, dismissal, transfer) - so within-specialty transfers likely INCLUDED; confirm in full text.

headline_rates.ACGME_all_specialty_comparator: mean 2.1%, decreasing from 3% (2009) to 1.6% (2019) [abstract wording ambiguous whether the decline refers to NS or all-ACGME rate]

key_findings: NS annual attrition higher than all-specialty ACGME mean. Mandatory 7-year training began 2013; 16 new programs (115 total).

attrition_definition: ACGME categories: transfers, withdrawal, dismissal ('did not graduate'). Within-specialty transfers INCLUDED.

headline_rates.by_PGY: PGY-specific transfer rates computed (values not in abstract)

method: Retrospective; retention assessed from public program information
attrition_definition: Retention at program per public listings (short follow-up). Handling of transfers not stated in abstract.

citation.authors: Raman HS, Limbrick DD, Ray WZ, Coble DW, Church S, Dacey RG, Zipfel GJ
citation.title: Prevalence, management, and outcome of problem residents among neurosurgical training programs in the United States

study_period: ~20-year program histories (mean 17.4 years of data per program)
data_source: Anonymous survey of program directors
method: PD survey; multivariable logistic regression for departure of problem residents
attrition_definition: Departure from the residency program (voluntary or terminated); terminated residents often trained in another NS program - i.e., program-level departure, includes transfers.

headline_rates.departures: 97 problem residents departed: 65% voluntary (mostly another specialty), 35% terminated
headline_rates.overall_program_attrition: surveyed but value not in abstract

key_findings: Departure predictors: dishonesty (OR 3.23), poor fund of knowledge (OR 2.54), poor technical skill (OR 2.37).
